current.title: The current regime
current.body: One answer to the day's most important question: is the market rewarding risk (Risk On), punishing it (Risk Off), or undecided (Neutral)? The gauge shows how confident the model is — trade smaller when confidence is low.

timeline.title: Regime timeline
timeline.body: The regime score over the last 60 sessions. Above the upper dashed line is Risk On territory, below the lower one is Risk Off. A score that keeps crossing the lines means an unstable, choppy market.

pillars.title: The five pillars
pillars.body: What the regime verdict is built from: trend, breadth, volatility, liquidity, and macro — each scored 0–100. When pillars disagree (say, trend bullish but breadth bearish), treat the overall regime with more caution.

flow.title: The rotation path
flow.body: Sectors ordered from where money is leaving to where it's arriving, based on 24-hour performance. Capital rarely exits crypto — it rotates. Riding the sector it's rotating into is usually easier than fighting the one it's leaving.

metrics.title: Flow quality
metrics.body: How strong the rotation is, how confident the model is that it's real (24h and 7d rankings agreeing), and the winning and losing sectors with their average 24-hour move. A high-confidence, persistent flow is far more tradeable than an unstable one.

heatmap.title: Sector heatmap

overview.title: Token overview
overview.body: Live price, 24-hour change and key stats for this token. Use the timeframe buttons (15M up to 1W) to change the chart — everything on this page recalculates for the timeframe you pick. The tiny dot above each button is that timeframe's bias (green = leans long, red = leans short, grey = neutral), so you can spot when a short-term bounce is fighting the bigger trend.

chart.title: Price chart
chart.body: Each candle is one period of price movement (green = closed up, red = closed down). The legend below the chart names every overlay — EMAs, support/resistance, swing points, trade-plan levels — and clicking a legend item hides or shows it (your choices are remembered). The trade-plan levels and zones always belong to your selected objective's trigger timeframe — the legend names it (e.g. 'Trade plan · 4H') — so exploring other chart timeframes never changes the plan. When your objective's verdict wants the trade, shaded zones appear: reward (green), risk (red), and the buy/sell pocket (blue). On 1H and higher timeframes the chart also marks true demand/supply bases — consolidations that launched an explosive move. Drag the chart left past the oldest candle to load more history.

insight.title: Key insight & components
insight.body: The market's condition in plain words — trend, momentum, volume, volatility — plus every check the engine ran. Green passed, amber is a caution, red failed.

objective.title: Start with your objective
objective.body: Tell the assistant what you're trying to do — a quick scalp, an intraday trade, a multi-day swing, or a weeks-long trend position. Each objective is judged on its own pair of timeframes (a bigger one for context, a smaller one for the trigger), so the same chart can favor a scalp while ruling out a swing. The dot is each objective's verdict at a glance, and picking one switches the chart to its trigger timeframe.

decision.title: A verdict for YOUR objective
decision.body: Not one answer for everyone: the assistant answers for the objective you picked — go, go at reduced size, not yet, or stand aside — with the plan levels and the one thing standing in the way, all on one screen. 'Not yet' is not 'never': the Why tab lists every missing confirmation and the price events that would flip today's verdict.

risk.title: Execution plan
risk.body: When your objective has a payable setup: entry, stop, profit targets, and a position sized from your account settings — automatically halved when the trade is counter-trend. When there's no plan, the assistant points at the objective that is payable instead.

chart.infoHint: Candlestick chart of the selected timeframe. The legend below the chart explains every overlay — click an item to hide or show it. Drag the chart past the oldest candle to load more history. The expand button opens the chart fullscreen.

header.inWatchlistTitle: In your watchlist — click to remove

phase.neitherContext: Neither {{ctxTf}} nor {{exeTf}} leans clearly either way — nothing to react to yet.
phase.counterTrendContext: Higher timeframe remains {{htf}}. Short-term momentum has shifted {{direction}} after a {{setup}}. Expect a {{move}} into {{zone}} before trend continuation.
phase.opportunityContext: {{ctxTf}} and {{exeTf}} agree {{direction}} — with-trend conditions, no conflicting higher-timeframe pull to fade.
phase.standbyContext: {{ctxTf}} leans {{direction}}, but {{exeTf}} hasn't confirmed the trigger yet — same direction, not tradable at current price.

assistant.title: Decision Assistant
assistant.infoHint: One chart, many valid answers. Pick your objective and the assistant tells you whether this market pays it right now, what confirmation is still missing, and which price events would change today's answer.

plan.executionInfoHint: A complete plan for your objective, sized to your account: entry, stop, two targets, position size, and worst-case loss. Counter-trend verdicts are automatically halved. Change account size and risk in Settings.
plan.setupInvalid: Setup no longer valid at current price.
plan.emptyExtendedWithPlan: No {{direction}} at current price — price is extended into structure. If it {{reaction}} to {{low}}–{{high}}, a {{direction}} becomes viable (see the conditional setup below).
plan.emptyExtended: No {{direction}} at current price — price is extended into structure. Wait for a pullback.
plan.emptyWait: No entry yet — the plan appears the moment the trigger confirms.
plan.emptyAvoid: This market doesn't pay your objective right now.
plan.emptyAlt: If you want action today, the {{objective}} objective has a {{size}}{{direction}} setup on the {{timeframe}}.
plan.emptyNoAlt: No other objective has a payable setup either — flat is a position.
plan.sizedFor: Sized for a ${{accountSize}} account risking {{riskPercent}}% per trade ({{stopMethod}} stop).
plan.halfSizeNote: Shown at half size — counter-trend for this objective.

why.verdictInfoHint: 'Not yet', 'reduced size', 'wrong direction', and 'unsuitable market' are all different answers. The Overview names the one that applies; this text explains why in plain words.
why.checklistInfoHint: Everything this objective needs before a full-size entry. The unchecked items are what 'not yet' means, concretely. Hover an item for the detail.
why.whatChangesInfoHint: Concrete price events that would upgrade, downgrade, or flip today's verdict — so you know what to watch for instead of re-reading the chart all day.
why.marketOutlookInfoHint: The current market story for this token, told before any recommendation: the big picture, the near-term tape, and what that combination rewards. Every verdict is this narrative applied to one objective.

hold.held: Verdict held {{heldFor}} — it stands until a trigger below fires, so it won't flicker between refreshes.

gauge.meaningFavored: Here the read and the entry conditions agree — the setup is confirmed.
gauge.meaningCaution: The read is tradable but fights the higher timeframe — hence reduced size.
gauge.meaningWait: A strong number beside 'not yet' is not a contradiction: the engine is confident about the direction while the entry conditions are still unsatisfied — the checklist shows exactly what's missing.
gauge.meaningAvoid: Whatever its strength, this market doesn't pay your objective — stand aside.
gauge.tooltipPrefix: How strongly the engine's evidence points in one direction — signal strength, not a win probability. The verdict word is the action.

decision.noEntryExtended: No entry at current price — {{missing}} of {{total}} confirmations missing
decision.planWhenZone: · plan appears once price returns to the zone
decision.planWhenTrigger: · plan appears once the trigger confirms
decision.flatIsPosition: No other objective is payable — flat is a position

leverage.title: Leverage
leverage.infoHint: Leverage doesn't change the risk-sized position — the same units and max loss hold. It only sets the margin you post and where you'd be liquidated. Keep leverage at or below 'Max safe' so your stop triggers before liquidation. Liquidation is an estimate; it excludes fees and funding.

liquidation.title: Liquidation vs invalidation
liquidation.danger: At {{leverage}}× liquidation ({{liq}}) triggers before your stop ({{stop}}) — you'd be liquidated before the idea is even invalidated. Drop to {{maxSafe}}× or lower so your stop does its job.
liquidation.thin: Liquidation ({{liq}}) sits only {{buffer}}% past your stop ({{stop}}) — a stop-run wick could liquidate you before the trade is invalidated. Consider {{maxSafe}}× or lower for more cushion.
liquidation.safe: Your stop ({{stop}}) triggers first; liquidation ({{liq}}) sits {{buffer}}% further out — a {{stops}}× stop-distance cushion. Invalidation stays in your control.

location.title: Entry Location
location.infoHint: Where price sits between support and resistance for this trade's direction. A long is best entered near support, a short near resistance — 'favored' is reserved for well-located setups, and an extended price becomes 'wait for a pullback' even when the direction is right.

session.title: Session Levels
session.infoHint: The high and low each trading region (Asia, London, New York) printed in its most recent completed session. Yesterday's session extremes are the intraday levels traders lean on — reclaiming a session high or holding a session low is a structure event. The level price is nearest is highlighted; the verdict's entry-location read counts a session level you're holding as structure.

sr.title: Support & Resistance · {{timeframe}}
sr.infoHint: Support is where buyers stepped in before (price floor); resistance is where sellers did (price ceiling). A long is best entered near support, a short near resistance.

details.marketReadInfoHint: What the two timeframes behind your objective are doing. When they disagree it doesn't mean 'no trade' — it changes which objectives are payable and which should wait.
details.conditionsInfoHint: The market's current condition in plain words — trend, momentum, volume, volatility, and the swing structure (higher or lower highs and lows) the engine reads from the chart — with the exact ATR and volume readings below. Bigger ATR means wilder swings.
details.engineChecksInfoHint: Every check the engine ran with its score contribution. Hover a check to read what it found. Green passed, amber is a caution, red failed.

perp.title: Perp Positioning
perp.infoHint: Funding + open interest — what perp traders check first. Positive funding means longs are paying to hold (crowded long, flush risk); negative means shorts are paying (crowded short, squeeze risk). Rising open interest means fresh money is behind the move; falling means positions are being closed. The verdict trims size when funding is extreme with the crowd already on your side.

drawer.infoHint: Requests a constitution-gated permit using this token's current execution plan. The backend rechecks account state and derives executable quantity from the persisted permit snapshot.

memo.riskPlan: - **Risk plan:** entry zone `{{entryLow}}–{{entryHigh}}`, stop `{{stop}}`, target 1 `{{target1}}`, target 2 `{{target2}}`

legend.candlesHint: One bar of price movement — green closed up, red closed down. The wicks show the high and low reached within the bar.

volume.label: Volume
volume.hint: Traded volume per bar along the bottom — green when the candle closed up, red when it closed down. Rising volume confirms a move; falling volume questions it.

emaFast.label: EMA {{length}}
emaFast.hint: Exponential moving average of the last 13 closes — the fast momentum curve. Price above it with EMA 13 on top of EMA 21 favors buyers.

emaSlow.label: EMA {{length}}
emaSlow.hint: Exponential moving average of the last 21 closes — the slower trend curve the fast EMA is measured against.

support.label: Support
support.hint: Dashed green trend line through recent swing lows — the floor buyers have been defending.

resistance.label: Resistance
resistance.hint: Dashed amber trend line through recent swing highs — the ceiling sellers have been defending.

pivots.label: Swing structure
pivots.hint: Arrows mark the confirmed swing legs (amber ▼ highs, green ▲ lows), each labeled against the prior swing of its kind: HH/HL = higher high/low, LH/LL = lower high/low. BOS tags a break that extends the trend; CHoCH a break against it — the first structural hint of a reversal. EQH/EQL mark equal highs/lows — matching swing levels where stop-loss liquidity tends to rest. Trend lines and setups are built from these.

liquidity.label: Liquidity
liquidity.hint: Dashed horizontal lines at intact liquidity pools: purple BSL (buy-side) at equal highs — stop orders resting above a double/triple top — and cyan SSL (sell-side) at equal lows. The label is the pool's strength tier — Strong/Moderate/Weak, from touches, tightness, and freshness — an ordinal ranking, not a probability. Price is often drawn toward these levels before reversing. Circles mark liquidity sweeps: a wick ran the pool's stops but the candle closed back inside — a stop hunt, and often the start of the move the raid funded.

plan.label: Trade plan
plan.hint: Your objective's plan levels: entry (blue), stop (rose), target 1 (solid green), target 2 (dashed green). These come from the objective's trigger timeframe (named on the label) and stay the same while you explore other chart timeframes — one trade story per page. Shown only while the objective has a directional plan.

zones.label: Trade zones
zones.hint: Shaded bands drawn only while your objective's verdict wants the trade: green = reward to target 1, red = risk to the stop, blue = the buy/sell pocket around entry. Like the trade plan, they belong to the objective's trigger timeframe (named on the label), whatever timeframe the chart shows.

sdZones.label: Demand/Supply
sdZones.hint: True demand/supply bases: a tight consolidation followed by an explosive move away. Green = demand (buyers launched from here), amber = supply (sellers did). Bright = fresh and untested; faded = already retested once. Zones price closed through are dropped. Detected on 1H, 4H, 1D and 1W charts, where bases are meaningful.

sessions.label: Session H/L
sessions.hint: The high and low of the most recent completed Asia (pink), London (teal) and New York (orange) session, drawn as dotted levels. Yesterday's session extremes are the intraday levels traders lean on. Shown on 15M–4H charts, where they're in range.

events.label: News & events
events.hint: Token news (past) and calendar catalysts (upcoming, ⧗) plotted on the bar they land on — coloured red/grey/green by likely impact (security, delisting, regulatory and unlocks read red; listings and upgrades green). Circles below a bar are past news; squares above the last bar are scheduled events. Click a marker for details and its source, or use the strip under the chart.
